title: Tiny chunk wastage and internal mempool inventory mismatch
content:
Summary:

This note collects field observations and early repro experiments around a subtle source of OOMs we keep seeing on small-batch, latency-sensitive infra: an internal mempool inventory mismatch that leads to many small leftover slots (tiny-chunk wastage) which prevent larger allocations from succeeding, triggering cudaMalloc fallbacks and visible retry storms. Goal is to capture what we measured, quick repro steps, telemetry we should add, and candidate mitigations to try in the short/medium term.

Why this matters (high level):
- Symptoms: intermittent OOMs during bursts with sequence-length variance; heap shows a lot of small free blocks that never coalesce; subsequent large allocation (workspace or KV-cache growth) fails and triggers slow path (cudaMalloc, retries, gatekeeper backoff) causing request latency spikes and sometimes host-side workload throttling.
- Impact: increased p99 latency, increased overall GPU utilization due to retry spin, lower effective concurrency because kernels/allocators serialize.
- Distinct from prior notes: unlike classic fragmentation from long-lived pinned tensors, this is an "inventory mismatch" between our internal mempool bookkeeping and what the device allocator thinks is free; often driven by allocator rounding, per-stream arenas, and small-buffer churn. We have many docs on slab and eviction — this focuses on the small-chunk combinatorics and the interaction with cudaMallocAsync fallback thresholds.

Field observations (logs / traces):
- Many small frees (8KiB, 16KiB, 32KiB) show up as frequently reused within a single worker, but free-list coalescing rarely happens; free-list remains high-cardinality.
- When a 1–2MiB workspace allocation requests, allocator walks fail to find contiguous region; we observe immediate attempt to satisfy via cudaMallocAsync reserved arenas; when occupancy is near threshold, process hits async fallback which triggers the expensive host path and introduces retries.
- Trace snippet (simplified):
  - t=0: burst of 64 concurrent small inferences -> many ephemeral small buffers (activations, attention scratch) allocated from per-stream arenas
  - t=25ms: buffers freed in different order -> gaps of 32KiB/64KiB in arena
  - t=40ms: model needs workspace 1.8MiB for large token path -> arena walk fails; attempt to extend into global mempool -> global mempool fragmented into 120+ small free blocks -> boundary fragments present
  - t=42ms: host-side cudaMalloc fallback invoked -> retry loop (log shows 3 retries with small exponential backoff) -> latency spike and occasional OOM after exceeding retry window

Hypothesis on root cause: inventory mismatch emerges from two interacting sources:
1) Rounding and bucketization: many small allocations are rounded up to allocation quantum that does not align with our coalescer size, so coalescing opportunities are missed.
2) Per-stream/per-thread arenas: short-lived allocations get returned to an arena local free-list that isn't globally coalesced. Free-order scattering causes fragmentation that global reclaim doesn't fix quickly. Additionally, our deferred-free path (to support async kernels) mixes freed blocks back into a reclamation queue; timing of reclamation can leave many small blocks in limbo during bursts.

Measurements we ran (quick reproducible tests):
- Microbench harness: synthetic workload that alternates 128x 16KiB alloc/free on random streams and occasionally issues a 2MiB alloc. Observed 85% failure to satisfy the 2MiB allocation within first attempt under default arena config.
- Heap snapshots: used our existing heap-exporter to capture free-list histograms before/after bursts. Free-list shape: 90% buckets below 64KiB, median free-run-length < 48KiB.
- Kernel occupancy correlation: spikes in cudaMalloc host fallback correlate with increased variance in sequence length (i.e., sudden shift from short to long token paths).

Telemetry we should add (short list prioritized):
- Free-run histogram per device and per pool (buckets: <16KiB, 16-64KiB, 64-256KiB, 256KiB-1MiB, >1MiB).
- Per-request allocator path taken (fast-path, arena alloc, global mempool, cudaMallocAsync fallback, host cudaMalloc) as tags in traces.
- Deferred-free queue length and average hold time.
- Coalescer success rate: count attempts to coalesce on free and how many merges resulted in larger blocks.
- Number of retries for each cudaMalloc fallback attempt with timings.
- Snapshot correlation: emit small trace sample whenever fallback_count > 0 (attach free-run histogram).

Quick mitigations to test (experimental ranking):
1) Immediate (low-risk): increase coalescer aggressiveness threshold for small buckets (merge adjacent <64KiB blocks more eagerly, even at slight CPU cost). Rollout to canary pool only.
2) Short-term (medium-risk): drain per-stream arena free-lists periodically when global larger requests are pending (triggered by observed large allocation requests). Implement as a synchronous fallback that attempts to return small freelist items to global pool before hitting global allocation path.
3) Mid-term (higher-risk): implement best-fit selection for large allocations to preferentially pick region with contiguous run-length; or add fragmentation-aware reservation (reserve contiguous slab for workspace on model start). More invasive and needs benchmark.
4) Long-term: allocator redesign to maintain a compacting/coalescing pass under low-load windows (opportunistic defragmentation) or introduce slab-allocator for workspace vs small-churn pools separation.

Reproducer steps (dev box):
1) Checkout PR branch: serving-runtime repro harness at (see linked PR) https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145
2) Run harness: ./repro -streams 8 -small-alloc-size 16384 -small-alloc-count 128 -large-alloc-size 1900000 -burst-interval 50 --duration 120
3) Capture heap via exporter every 5s: /scripts/heap-dump.sh --out out/heap-$(timestamp).json
4) Check logs for "fallback->host cudaMalloc" messages and count retries.

Open experiments to run (owned by Marco/Elena):
- E1: Aggressive coalescing (toggle param) on canary p4d nodes. Measure p50/p95 latency and fallback_count. Compare token-level QoS.
- E2: Arena drain play: when large alloc requested, invoke arena.drain_to_global(limit=1MB) and observe success rate of large allocs. Measure overhead.
- E3: Time-based deferred-free flush: reduce deferred-free latency window from current 200ms to 40ms in a canary to reduce limbo. Observe if that reduces tiny-chunk inventory during bursts.

Risks and unknowns:
- More aggressive coalescing may increase CPU overhead and contention on the global free-list lock. Need to measure lock contention telemetry.
- Arena drain might increase churn across global pool causing different fragmentation pattern; could harm steady-state throughput.
- Changing deferred-free timing might break correctness in some edge-case async kernel completion ordering; need thorough tests.

Next steps / checklist:
- [ ] Add the telemetry items above to the allocator instrumentation (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Ship microbench harness improvements and CI reproducer (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Implement aggressive coalescer flag as runtime param and test in canary pool (owner: Elena)
- [ ] Run E1/E2/E3 and collect metrics into experiment dashboard; follow-up decision meeting.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Could try a hybrid approach: small-churn pool for ephemeral tensors and a reserved workspace slab for large allocations; that feels safest but requires config heuristics per-model.
- Correlate with SLO incidents tags: JIRA-INV-3321 has two recent incidents; attach heap dumps.

Attachments / snippets:
- Heap histogram sample (pasted to Confluence page): confluence:workspace-sizing-rationale
- Repro harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145

If anyone has recent heap dumps from p99 incidents (Nov-Dec 2024) please drop into out/heap-dumps/ under the experiment bucket; those files will help confirm whether this is the same pattern we've been chasing.

-- Priya
